title: Request Lifecycle
markdown:
A single chat message makes a full round-trip through the API, the orchestrator's tool-use loop, a parallel specialist fan-out, and synthesis — all streamed back as server-sent events.

### Steps

1. **Arrival** — the client mints a `client_turn_id` and posts to `POST /chat` (`openexecutive.api.routes.chat`). The turn carries a `<current_speaker>` hint resolved from the caller's `person_id` (followed by that person's `<working_style>` rules when they have any — see the attunement section), plus a `<briefing>` digest of current open alerts (built in parallel with RAG/episodic/peer-memory fetches) so the Executive can discuss any item shown on the `/today` briefing page. A turn arriving from a chat adapter instead of the web app also carries a `<channel>` block naming the surface and stating which approvals can be completed there; on Slack the `<briefing>` digest is gated to the principal's DMs. All three ride in the **user turn**, never a cached system block. The server registers a stop switch under that id *before* the context fetch, so a Stop pressed during those first seconds halts the turn before any model call is made.
2. **Tool-use loop** — the `Executive` calls Claude. For a cross-domain question the assistant turn emits multiple `consult_specialist` tool-use blocks at once.
3. **Parallel fan-out** — `openexecutive.orchestrator.router.route_parallel` dispatches those calls concurrently, bounded by `MAX_PARALLEL_SPECIALISTS`; calls past the cap get a skip tool_result.
4. **Per-specialist RAG** — each specialist runs its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query, then reasons over the retrieved chunks and returns analysis as a tool_result.
5. **Synthesis** — the Executive feeds the tool_results back to Claude and streams one coherent reply. Every tool round — not just a specialist one — emits an `activity` event naming what is running, immediately followed by a `thinking` keepalive. The label names the *activity*, never the internal agent: "Putting time on the calendar…", "Looking up people…", or, for an MCP call, the underlying tool by name. A round that really does fan out collapses to the generic "Consulting specialists…" — the one voice holds even in the progress line. The keepalive carries no tool information of its own; it used to drive a hardcoded "Consulting specialists…" string, so an MCP or calendar round misreported itself as a fan-out.
6. **Optional committee review** — when enabled, `Executive.stream_chat_with_committee()` runs a silent draft, parallel reviewer critiques, then a streamed revision pass.
7. **Side effects** — after the reply, every rostered speaker's turn (not only the principal's) schedules a fire-and-forget **open-loop pass** (Attunement) beside the episodic extraction: a keyword prefilter, then one forced-tool call that may open or close loops, every item quote-gated against the speaker's own words. The user message is persisted with `sender_person_id` — the resolved speaker, never the principal fallback a Discord / Telegram session uses for ownership — and the session records the speaker for the turn (`Session.caller_person_id`), which `close_open_loop` reads. A DM sent while proactive work is tagged (`attunement.outcomes.tag_proactive` — scheduler dispatch, reflection, research, alert review) also opens an outcome-ledger row at `_record_outbound_context`; a user's own turn is never tagged. Any side-effecting tool call surfaces an `action_taken` chip, which unlike the ephemeral `activity` label is persisted with the assistant message; the stream closes with a `done` event — preceded by a `stopped` event when the user halted the turn, in which case the partial reply is still persisted and flagged so it reads as cut short rather than complete, and is mirrored into the live in-memory session so the next turn's prompt matches what was saved. The stream still ends with `done` event. One side-effecting tool is gated server-side rather than by its description: `ack_alert` will only accept an `alert_id` from the live alert board the server itself derived this turn — the whole live set, not only the rows the `<briefing>` digest printed, since `/today` renders more cards than the digest lists and every one of them is Discuss-able — and it fails closed, so an id it cannot even parse is refused rather than waved through to the handler's own parse. That check runs on **every** session. It used to run only on turns that arrived from a chat channel, keyed on `origin_channel`, which the browser never sets — so the web, the surface the principal actually uses, was unchecked and the model could ack any id, including one quoted out of an alert body by the briefing page's Discuss handoff. What that buys is bounded and worth stating plainly: an id that is invented, closed, snoozed or expired is refused, including one quoted out of an attacker-written alert body; the model being argued into acking the wrong *live* card is not prevented. The board is recorded on the turn's `Session`, and the route binds that session for the **whole** SSE body (`schedule_tools.set_session`, alongside `set_turn`) rather than letting `stream_chat` bind it from inside its own generator. `_sse_body` drives the executive with `asyncio.wait_for(stream.__anext__())`, which runs each step in a fresh Task holding a *copy* of the context, so a binding made inside the generator is discarded with the step that made it: step one sees the session and every later step sees `None`. The tool-call loop runs on those later steps, so the whole guard read an empty set and refused every ack on the web — on live, open cards — until the binding moved out to the route. Anything reading `current_session` mid-turn has the same requirement, and two of them needed more than the binding to behave. `schedule_followup`'s seen-`channel_ref` anti-spam gate refuses a send to an address the session has not seen; with no session it skipped itself, so a web turn could schedule to **any** address, and with an empty one it refused even the principal's own. The route now seeds the caller's own addresses onto the session, so on web the gate means what it means on every other surface. Reply linkage (`_record_outbound_context`, read back by `inbound_hydration` to quote the originating conversation into the turn handling a recipient's reply) is the other: it was never reachable on web, and rather than switch that on for the principal's broadest surface as a side effect it is held back, keyed on an explicit `Session.from_web_chat` flag. Not on an empty `origin_channel` — that names an inbound chat adapter, and the email poller, alert review, the CLI and the unattended workflows all leave it empty while legitimately recording linkage. `scheduled_actions` rows also take their `session_id` from the session. A session that was shown no board has an empty trusted set and can ack nothing, so the unattended passes (the nightly reflection, the research synthesis) are refused by default — they also still withhold the tool outright, which is belt-and-braces rather than the only thing stopping them. After the stream closes, the turn is also handed to the episodic memory extractor (`memory.episodic.schedule_extraction`, fire-and-forget) — on every turn where the principal said anything at all, and only the principal: a turn naming an `origin_channel` must resolve to a person marked `is_principal`, because the quote validator downstream cannot tell whose words it is checking. Both this path and the committee path call the same `should_extract` predicate, and it applies no length floor: the gate used to sum in the assistant's reply, which let a verbose answer drag a trivial turn in and discarded the short, decisive instructions that are the whole point of extracting. A user-side floor would fare no better — "Do B." and "Done" are one character apart. See **Memory** for what that cost on a live tenant.
8. **Tool failures** — a handler that raises instead of returning its JSON error is isolated: both tool gathers run with `return_exceptions=True`, the model gets an error `tool_result` naming only the exception's TYPE — a message can carry a filesystem path, a validation error echoing the input, or a third-party HTTP body, and anything in model context can be quoted back to the user, so the full repr stays in the log and the audit row — and the failure is audited with `ok=false`. Only `CancelledError` is re-raised, so turn-timeout and client-disconnect handling still work. Before this one crashing tool aborted the whole turn, which reached the user as an unexplained apology with no audit row (#136).

Web search, when invoked on the Anthropic path, executes inside the Anthropic API itself (`web_search_20250305`) and returns within the same generation; for any model routed via OpenRouter the same tool becomes OpenRouter's `openrouter:web_search` server tool, which also runs inside the generation with the same search cap and domain lists.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant API as FastAPI /chat
  participant E as Executive
  participant CL as Claude
  participant S as Specialists
  participant KB as ChromaDB
  C->>API: POST /chat message
  API->>E: start turn
  E->>CL: messages (tool-use loop)
  CL-->>E: consult_specialist calls
  E->>S: route_parallel fan-out
  S->>KB: domain-filtered RAG
  KB-->>S: chunks
  S-->>E: analysis tool_results
  E->>CL: synthesize
  CL-->>E: streamed reply
  E-->>API: SSE chunks then done
  API-->>C: streamed response
